what_happened.line: The Planning Board took no votes beyond adjournment and left a state planning grant for MBTA Communities zoning compliance unresolved.
Members were divided on the tone to take toward MBTA zoning, and one worried that opposing the process could put other town funding at risk.
The director described a grant that needs a match, which can be met partly with in-kind services, and would fund a consultant for early compliance work.
The director is drafting the master plan RFP for board review by end of June, aiming for the state central register in August.
The director is to confirm that the select board step on a Chapter land conveyance was executed, with back taxes figured on the area actually conveyed.

why_it_matters: Whether the town applies for the grant decides if it has outside help meeting MBTA Communities zoning rules, which a member linked to other state money the town may seek.
The master plan RFP is the next step in spending the money town meeting provided, and it will shape what residents are later asked to vote on.
watch_next: The May 23 Planning Board meeting, where the director is to confirm the land conveyance step and hearings on the Northfield land, the warehouse and cannabis retail are expected.
The draft master plan RFP, due to the board by the end of June.
